question: After 1500 cycles, what capacity does the cathode deliver per gram of sulfur and per gram of the whole electrode, and what sulfur share of the electrode does their ratio imply, against the sulfur content the paper states?
expect: 306 mAh/gS and 87 mAh/g electrode (p5.L103-105): ratio 28.4%; the stated loading is 35 wt% sulfur (in the carbon-sulfur composite)
rendered:
According to the paper, after 1500 cycles at 1C, the cathode delivers 306 mAh/gS of capacity per gram of sulfur. The whole electrode contains 35 wt% sulfur, so the ratio of capacity per gram of sulfur to capacity per gram of the whole electrode is 306/0.35 = 873 mAh/g. 

The paper states that the whole electrode delivers 87 mAh/g after 1500 cycles at 100% depth of discharge (DOD). This is a mass-specific performance, and it is not clear whether this value is per gram of sulfur or per gram of the whole electrode. However, since the ratio of capacity per gram of sulfur to capacity per gram of the whole electrode is 873 mAh/g, we can divide the mass-specific performance of the whole electrode (87 mAh/g) by 873 mAh/g to get the mass-specific performance per gram of sulfur, which is approximately 0.1 mAh/g. This is a very low value, and it is not clear how to interpret it.
